title: PFM Automotive review proposal
illustration: Illustrative visual - not a measurement result
truth: Draft for review - no customer data or live integrations

scenes.title: Turn showroom insight into commercial action.
scenes.intro: Identify contact gaps. Respond. Evaluate what changes.
scenes.body: Give the dealer a practical view of where contact opportunities are missed, when staff coverage is stretched and how model exploration progresses towards registered follow-up.
scenes.question: Where could better timing or follow-up improve your showroom process?
scenes.detail: PFM combines measurement design, operational insight and dealer reviews. Commercial improvement is the goal; demonstrated results require a baseline and comparable follow-up.
scenes.alt: Illustrative showroom with vehicle zones, visitors, a sales desk and service reception.

scenes.title: How many people enter?
scenes.intro: A reliable baseline starts at the entrance.
scenes.body: Count entries and exits at each selected entrance and time window. Distinguish people, repeat crossings and derived visits. Group detection is a separate analysis that requires validation.
scenes.question: Which entrances and opening hours should be included?
scenes.detail: Proposed entrance options: Xovis or Milesight. Product selection, coverage and staff exclusion require a site assessment.
scenes.alt: Illustrative arrival of individual visitors and groups in a car showroom.

scenes.title: Which destinations do visitors reach?
scenes.intro: Showroom, service and reception each have a distinct role.
scenes.body: Show which defined zones are reached and how journeys continue. Reaching a service zone identifies a destination; it does not establish why someone entered.
scenes.question: Can we define zones and visit purposes separately?
scenes.detail: A confirmed service purpose requires additional appointment or registration data. Keep mixed-purpose and unknown visits visible.
scenes.source: Physical routes + dealer floor plan → derived insight
scenes.alt: Illustrative showroom routes towards service, reception and the sales area.

scenes.title: How do visitors move from model to model?
scenes.intro: Explore the route through the showroom.
scenes.body: Follow transitions between model zones within validated measurement coverage. Show which combinations occur, without presenting a route as personal preference or purchase intent.
scenes.question: Which model zones and transitions matter to the dealer?
scenes.detail: Proposed deeper analysis: LiDAR or a suitable Xovis 3D configuration. Sensor handover, obstructions and sight lines require validation.
scenes.source: Physical trajectories + model zones → derived insight
scenes.alt: Illustrative overhead view of a route between vehicle zones in a showroom.

scenes.title: Which models do visitors spend time near?
scenes.intro: See model dwell patterns and identify where to investigate.
scenes.body: Compare zone reach and dwell time to test model placement and campaign focus. A configured dwell threshold can flag a contact opportunity; it does not establish purchase intent.
scenes.question: Which models need a different placement or more timely staff coverage?
scenes.detail: Define zone boundaries, minimum dwell time, return visits and passing trajectories before showing model comparisons.
scenes.source: Physical zone events + model layout → derived insight
scenes.alt: Illustrative visitors in defined zones around showroom vehicles.

scenes.title: Who leaves without a contact signal?
scenes.intro: Make potential contact gaps visible while there is still time to respond.
scenes.body: Separate qualifying visits with contact, visitors still present without contact and completed visits without a detected contact indicator. Use these groups to investigate coverage and improve the greeting process.
scenes.question: Where should a salesperson respond sooner?
scenes.detail: Qualifying means a validated dwell rule, not a proven buyer. Contact requires validated staff distinction and proximity/duration rules; no detected signal does not prove no conversation occurred.
scenes.source: Physical trajectories + staff distinction → derived insight
scenes.alt: Illustration of visitors and a salesperson beside a showroom vehicle, with purple markers.

scenes.title: Does the visit reach the sales desk?
scenes.intro: From the showroom floor to the next observable step.
scenes.body: Measure presence in the agreed desk zone and examine progression after contact signals. Sitting at a desk does not prove a quotation, lead or sale.
scenes.question: Which desk zones and follow-up actions should we track separately?
scenes.detail: A contact-to-desk rate requires the same valid trajectories and observation period. A quotation requires a separate CRM or DMS record.
scenes.source: Physical desk zone + zone definitions → derived insight
scenes.alt: Illustrative showroom with model exploration on the left and visitors at a sales desk on the right.

scenes.title: What changes after a campaign or process change?
scenes.intro: Connect showroom patterns with marketing and registered follow-up.
scenes.body: Compare campaign dates, visit volumes, model-zone dwell and contact coverage. Add CRM/DMS leads, quotations and orders to review the process with the dealer.
scenes.question: Which campaign or operational change should we evaluate first?
scenes.detail: Keep source periods, channels and definitions aligned. Without valid visit-cohort linkage, CRM totals remain separate series. Campaign association is not proof of campaign impact.
scenes.alt: Conceptual illustration of showroom contact and commercial records; not a measured funnel.

scenes.title: Which measurement design fits your question?
scenes.body: Select entrance counting, showroom zones, validated staff distinction and an alert workflow. Add staffing schedules, campaign calendars and permitted CRM/DMS links where the chosen question needs them.
scenes.question: Which measurement, response and review workflow should we configure?
scenes.detail: Phone or smartwatch alerts are available according to supplied product input, subject to a compatible delivery channel, configured rule and operational ownership. No notification or integration is triggered by this review.
scenes.source: Proposed scope for a site assessment
scenes.alt: Illustrative showroom with different measurement areas for a proposed measurement design.

scenes.title: From insight to action to evaluated results.
scenes.intro: Agree the response, the owner and the evidence of change.
scenes.body: Test a greeting alert, adjust peak-hour coverage or review campaign follow-up. PFM and the dealer agree a baseline, action owner and evaluation date, then compare contact and commercial indicators.
scenes.question: Next step: choose one improvement experiment and a review date.
scenes.detail: Compare matched periods and sufficiently mature cohorts, accounting for channel mix, staffing and seasonality. Describe observed change first; claim impact only when the evaluation supports it. System actions in this review are simulated.
scenes.alt: Illustrative meeting between showroom visitors and a member of staff.

geo.title: Where does showroom demand come from?
geo.intro: Add origin areas, brand-related visitation patterns and aggregate visits to other showrooms when a suitable source supports the analysis. These describe a panel or modelled population, not every visitor counted at the entrance.

articles.title: Origins and reach
articles.body: Use aggregate origin areas with the source population, period and area definition visible. Do not link an individual origin to a sensor trajectory.

articles.title: Affinity and other showrooms
articles.body: Visits to brand-related locations are a contextual signal. The term brand affinity requires an explicit provider definition; it does not establish preference, ownership or purchase intent.

geo.note: Availability, representativeness, minimum counts and location attribution must be confirmed with the data provider. This proposal therefore contains no map or fictional percentages for this analysis.

review.title: Review before implementation
items: Does the story make the dealer value clear: contact gaps, timely response and evaluated improvement?
Which alert channels, recipients and escalation rules fit the dealer’s operation?
Which staffing, model-presentation or campaign question should be tested first?
Which group, contact and CRM cohort definitions can be validated?
Do the proposed visuals and illustrative output reflect what PFM can deliver in the selected scope?
review.note: The existing brochure has not been changed. No customer results, prices, uplift, benchmarks or live system actions have been added to this proposal.

output.title: What do we get?
output.intro: An illustrative showroom performance view for daily prioritisation and dealer review.
output.scope: Northstar Retail Group | Showroom A | 5 Nov 2026 | 09:00-14:05 CET | Illustrative snapshot
output.definition: Unit: deduplicated person-visits, not groups or identified people. Qualifying: at least 60 seconds in a model zone; example rule, not buying intent. Contact: validated staff-contact indicator.
output.reconciliation: 68 qualifying visits = 40 with contact + 22 departed without a detected contact signal + 6 still present without a detected contact signal. Contact coverage = 40 / 68 = 58.8%, rounded to 59%.
output.crmBody: 7 quotations | 3 orders. Illustrative registrations during the reporting day. These are separate totals, not conversions from today’s visit cohort.
output.alertBody: Model zone 4: dwell 2m 05s, no detected contact signal. Example alert threshold: 90s. Route to a configured phone or smartwatch; no message is sent here.
actions: Coverage: compare visit demand, contact signals and available staff by time window.
Model presentation: investigate dwell and coverage by zone before changing the layout.
Marketing: align campaign dates and channels with showroom patterns and CRM follow-up.
output.note: Fictional output specimen inspired by the supplied dashboard; the values are independently created fixtures. No customer data, benchmark, live feed or guaranteed product screen. CRM snapshot: 14:00 CET; physical snapshot: 14:05 CET.

action.title: Act during the visit. Learn after the change.
action.intro: Operational alerts and structured dealer reviews turn measurement into a repeatable improvement process.

articles.title: Respond to a contact opportunity
articles.body: A configured dwell-without-contact rule can trigger a phone or smartwatch notification. Assign an available recipient, acknowledge the alert, provide cover and review the response.
articles.detail: Product input: alerts are already possible. Confirm channel compatibility, staff distinction, zones, latency, repeat-alert suppression and escalation for the selected deployment. This example is simulated.

articles.title: Improve coverage and model presentation
articles.body: Use busy time windows, time to first contact and zone dwell to choose a staffing or layout experiment. Give the action an owner and compare the same definitions before and after.
articles.detail: Keep visits without a contact signal visible. Interpret time to contact among contacted visits separately. A longer model dwell is not proven interest.

articles.title: Evaluate marketing and commercial follow-up
articles.body: Combine campaign calendars, channel tags and approved CRM/DMS records with aggregate showroom patterns. Review whether visits, model dwell, contacts and registered follow-up change together.
articles.detail: Use consented or otherwise permitted linkage, deduplication and a fixed outcome horizon. Without linkage, compare aggregate series; do not attribute individual orders or claim causal uplift.

action.note: Agree a baseline, action log and review date. Demonstrated results require comparable evidence; increased sales, ROI and payback are not promised.
